name: Lunar Fungus
summary: In Darkshore's caves, druids gather Lunar Fungus to help heal sick deer. Mixed with Earthroot and water, it strengthens a healing salve.

sections.title: Properties and Ecology
sections.body: Lunar Fungus grows from Lunar Fungal Blooms in Darkshore's underground caverns. The Cenarion Circle values its power to strengthen remedies. Mixed with soothing water and common Earthroot, it lends strength to a salve that counters debilitating afflictions. Territorial moonkin frequent the damp caves, so gathering the fungus takes care.

sections.title: A Lesson in Healing
sections.body: In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong has young druids gather Lunar Fungus as they study nature's healing arts. They learn how physical ingredients such as the fungus can counter poisons in local deer. By studying herbal remedies, initiates prepare to channel natural antidotes through shapeshifting and spiritual power.

faq.q: What is Lunar Fungus used for?
faq.answer: Lunar Fungus strengthens a healing salve. Alanndarian Nightsong mixes it with Earthroot and clean water to treat sick deer in Darkshore.
Lunar Fungus grows from Lunar Fungal Blooms in caves east of Auberdine, in Darkshore. Irritable moonkin share these caverns and defend their territory from intruders.

faq.q: Who requires this fungus in Auberdine?
faq.answer: Alanndarian Nightsong asks students of the wild to gather Lunar Fungus as part of their training. The fungus goes into remedies for ailing forest animals.

faq.q: Why do druid initiates have to gather physical herbs to cure poison?
faq.answer: Learning how physical antidotes work is a fundamental part of druidic education. Gathering herbs such as Lunar Fungus and seeing how they counter toxins teaches students the principles of healing before they learn to purge poison through spiritual magic.

angles.text: As a young druid, you seek Lunar Fungus in Darkshore's caves as part of your early training in curative magic and healing poisoned wildlife.
As a night elf, you help tend corrupted woodland creatures around Auberdine with native remedies such as Lunar Fungus.
